review_notes:
Midwood Barbers is the booking app for one two-chair barbershop at 2915 The Plaza, Villa Heights, Charlotte, NC.

Answers to the points raised under Guideline 2.1 follow, numbered as they were asked.

No account, login or registration exists anywhere in the app, so no demo credentials are needed. No in-app purchases, no subscriptions, no advertising, no analytics, no third-party SDKs. The app requests no permissions at all — no location, camera, contacts, notifications or App Tracking Transparency — and no permission prompt appears at any point in the walkthrough below.

2. DEVICES AND OPERATING SYSTEMS TESTED
[TO FILL IN: the physical iPhone models and iOS versions this build was run on before submission.] Minimum supported version is iOS 15.6; the app is iPhone-only and portrait-first.

3. WHAT THE APP DOES, AND FOR WHOM
It is for the customers of this one shop. A two-chair barbershop has nobody free to answer the phone while both chairs are busy, so booking means calling back or walking in and hoping. The app puts the whole board in the customer's hand: the menu with prices and lengths, the five days the shop opens, every free chair for the coming fortnight, and the record of visits already had.

4. SETTING UP AND REACHING EVERY FEATURE
There is nothing to set up: no credentials, no sample files, no configuration. A fresh install opens straight onto Home.
1. Home leads with the soonest free chair for the house Haircut ($40, 45 min) and how many of the two chairs are open then. "Take This Chair" opens the planner.
2. Services lists all seven across Cuts, Razor Work and Quick Work — Haircut $40, Skin Fade $45, Kids Cut $30, Straight Razor Shave $45, Beard Trim $25, Cut & Beard $60, Line-up $18 — each with its length and soonest opening. Tap any one.
3. In the planner, pick a day from the two-week strip. Sunday and Monday are struck through and cannot be tapped: the shop is shut. Tuesday to Friday run 10am–7pm, Saturday 10am–5pm.
4. The day below is a column of half hours. Taken times are struck through; free ones show whether one or both chairs are open. Tap a free time to hold it. A 75-minute Cut & Beard fits far fewer times than a 15-minute Line-up.
5. Visits lists what is held as ticket stubs, and gives a chair back.
6. Shop shows the week's hours, the address, a fixed non-interactive map pin, and buttons for Directions and Call.
7. Reviews shows the shop's overall public standing, and lets a past visit be rated one to five stars with an optional private note.

5. EXTERNAL SERVICES USED TO DELIVER CORE FUNCTIONALITY
None. The menu, prices, durations and opening hours are compiled into the app. No data provider, authentication service, payment processor, AI service or third-party backend takes any part in making a booking. Three buttons hand off to the operating system: Directions opens the address in Apple Maps, Call opens the dialler, and the reviews link opens the shop's public listing in the browser. The Privacy Policy row opens the published policy page in an in-app web view.

6. REGIONAL DIFFERENCES
None. One English (US) build, one shop, US prices and hours. Every feature behaves identically in every region, and nothing is gated by country, carrier or store front.

7. REGULATED INDUSTRY AND THIRD-PARTY MATERIAL
Barbering is not a regulated category and the app makes no health, medical or financial claim. All artwork, icons and copy are original to this app. The Reviews tab prints the shop's standing as a single figure and links out to the listing; no third-party review text, reviewer name or photograph is reproduced. A star rating and note a customer leaves is their own record, never published or shown to anyone else, so the app carries no user-generated content feed and needs no reporting or blocking mechanism.
